subject.title: Embedded agent: auto-rotate (or persist a marker) on context-overflow give_up instead of wedging the session until manual /reset

question: Should exhausted embedded-agent context-overflow recovery persist a durable blocked-overflow state, auto-rotate and replay the pending turn once, or keep manual recovery with stronger visibility?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally preserve the session mapping with manual recovery, while the request changes core session recovery, replay safety, and durable session-state semantics for autonomous agents.

options.title: Persist blocked state first
options.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked marker plus visible operator recovery affordance without silently replaying a pending turn on a new session.

options.title: Guarded one-shot rotation
options.body: Rotate and replay once only after compaction and truncation are exhausted, with replay-safety gates and a per-session loop cap.

options.title: Keep manual recovery
options.body: Keep the documented `/reset` or `/new` contract and improve only diagnostics, surfacing, or docs.

recommendation.title: Persist blocked state first
recommendation.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked marker plus visible operator recovery affordance without silently replaying a pending turn on a new session.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history in overflow recovery and embedded-runner retry semantics among the likely owners inspected.
